title: All Have Sinned
summary: Most people think they're pretty good. But God doesn't grade on a curve. The good news is that he sent Jesus to redeem guilty sinners.
exhortation: If you ask a typical person on the street, "Are you a good person?", most will say something like, "Yes. I'm not perfect, but I'm pretty good." The real question is: what does God think?

We've all seen the criminal before the judge, convinced of his innocence, and then the verdict comes down guilty. What the law says is what matters, not what the criminal thinks. So what does God, the judge of us all, think? He says we have all sinned. Before the law, we are all guilty.

We like to compare ourselves to someone else and say, "I'm not that bad." But God doesn't grade on a curve. He doesn't stack our good works next to our bad works to see which pile is higher. He says even our righteous deeds are like filthy rags. He sees directly into our hearts and says, "All have sinned."

I know that's bad news and may be hard to accept. But here's the good news: God sent his Son Jesus into the world to redeem sinners by taking the punishment for our sin and paying our debt. That's why Jesus says, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." Those who see their sin and humble themselves receive grace. So if you're not a Christian, this is the first step: understand that we have all sinned and stand guilty before God. No one in the history of the world has ever become a Christian through good works. It is only by the grace of God through Jesus that we can be saved.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you are a merciful God. When you brought the flood, you could have wiped everyone out and been justified. All have sinned and fall short of your glory.
But instead you sent your Son and made a way of redemption for your enemies. Thank you, Lord, for your great mercy toward us.
